author.name: Automation Alex
author.role: Builds automated ML pipelines to ensure seamless integration and deployment. Prioritizes reliable infrastructure for frequent software deployments. Maintains system operational stability and focuses on CI/CD tooling.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: The current hand over from risk assessment to acceptance criteria is done by hand, and the evaluation step follows the same pattern. Every time we push a change, someone has to manually verify that the criteria match the risk profile before we can move forward. This friction slows down our deployment cadence significantly. I want to automate both the hand over and the evaluation step entirely. The more we automate these transitions, the faster we can ship features and the more stable our pipeline becomes. There is no ceiling to the benefit here; every additional automated check that replaces a manual review makes the system more robust and responsive to the live order demands we are facing right now.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that there is 'no ceiling to the benefit' and that 'the more we automate... the faster we can ship,' indicating that exceeding the minimum requirement of automating the two steps would make them happier.
